original_analysis.analysis_summary: The log set consists primarily of Sysmon ProcessAccess (EventID 10) and ImageLoad (EventID 7) events, routine Windows Security auditing events (5158, 5156, 4672, 4624, 4627, 4634, 4673) and normal Azure VM network activity. No evidence of malicious PowerShell commands, encoded payloads, or abnormal lateral movement was found. Registry modifications observed (e.g., VFUProvider) align with standard Windows security components. Privilege‑use audit failures (EventID 4673) are benign attempts by the LOCAL SERVICE account and did not result in a successful exploit. Consequently, the activity appears consistent with normal system operation.
original_analysis.agent_reasoning: 1. Identified log types: Sysmon (ProcessAccess, ImageLoad), Windows Security (Filtering Platform, Logon, Privilege Use). 2. Validated each EventID using the event_id_extractor tool (10, 7, 5158, 5156, 4672, 4624, 4627, 4634, 4673). 3. Reviewed ProcessAccess events – svchost.exe accessing other system processes (sihost.exe, explorer.exe, svchost.exe) with typical access masks (0x2000, 0x1000, 0x3000). These are expected for system services. 4. ImageLoad events show signed Microsoft DLLs (wmidcom.dll, dpapi.dll, perfos.dll) – all properly signed and trusted. 5. Network events (5158/5156) show guestagent.exe and other services connecting to Azure metadata endpoint (168.63.129.16:80) and local bind operations – normal for Azure VMs. 6. Registry events (CreateKey, SetValue) involve standard keys (Internet Settings, Tcpip Parameters, VFUProvider). No suspicious or unexpected keys were created. 7. Security events: 4672 (special privileges) and 4624/4627/4634 (logon/logoff) correspond to the computer account MORDORDC$ starting services – expected. 8. Audit failure 4673 (SeProfileSingleProcessPrivilege) is a benign failed privilege request by LOCAL SERVICE; no escalation succeeded. 9. No encoded PowerShell commands or anomalous file creations were detected. 10. Timeline building around the most active process (PID 2064) returned no additional suspicious sequence. Overall, the observed behavior matches normal Windows and Azure VM operation.
